review_output: {"summary":"Based only on the supplied snapshot, I found no BLOCKER and no remaining local MAJOR. The new safeguards are sound for the cases they cover. statement_timeout puts a limit on each statement and is fail-closed. row_security=off makes RLS filtering raise 42501 instead of silently skipping rows. The expected/touched count guard caught a real BEFORE-trigger skip with 23514 and rolled back. The previous unbounded-touch MAJOR is now a MINOR about bounds and capacity: each statement has a time limit, but total lock time and trigger-queue memory don't, and there is only one 100k data point. Remaining risks are in validation fidelity: the populated-DB deploy path through Prisma with a non-superuser role, the timeout failure and recovery path, the narrow P2034 attribution, and untested claims about ACL and lock release. Production capacity and trigger memory are not certified. The synchronized gate stays at 7/20 FAIL, and the full WP is NOT READY.","findings":[{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Deploy-path fidelity","file":"scripts/wp20-order-upgrade-load-disposable.mjs","issue":"The populated upgrade ran through psql -f as the postgres superuser, one statement at a time. The real path, Prisma migrate deploy, was not run on a populated DB: different role, different statement batching, a _prisma_migrations row, and failed-migration (P3009) recovery. The timeout abort path (57014) was never triggered.","evidence":"Load L61 runs docker exec psql -U postgres. The stated limitation is that main ran migrate deploy on an empty DB. No test forces 57014.","impact":"Problems with the deploy role (lock, function ownership, RLS) or the fail-and-recover flow could first appear at release.","recommended_fix":"In a disposable DB, migrate to 116, seed the data, then run prisma migrate deploy with a non-superuser role that matches the migration role.","required_test":"Successful deploy records 117 as finished. A test-only pg_sleep trigger forces 57014, then verify full rollback, the failed 117 row, migrate resolve, and that a redeploy succeeds.","confidence":0.8},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Bounds / capacity","file":"prisma/migrations/20261016050000_live_metric_order_upgrade_snapshot_fence/migration.sql","issue":"Each statement has a 30s limit, so the worst-case lock hold is roughly 5s plus 30s per statement, plus COMMIT. Trigger-queue memory has no limit. There is only one 100k point, so the row count at which it times out is unknown.","evidence":"L4-7 and L36-51. The receipt shows triggerQueuePeakMemory NOT_MEASURED and productionScale UNKNOWN.","impact":"At an unknown scale, deploy will fail closed or hit memory pressure. This is safe for data but blocks the release.","recommended_fix":"Run a local scaling series and use it to set a written limit on linked-payment count, to be checked by the future authorized Production preflight.","required_test":"Disposable runs at 100k, 500k and 1M that record migrationMs, WAL, backend memory (pg_backend_memory_contexts/log) and the 57014 threshold.","confidence":0.75},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Snapshot regression attribution","file":"scripts/wp20-order-upgrade-snapshot-disposable.mjs","issue":"P2034 is accepted as a general error code. It can also mean deadlock, and nothing checks that it came from the stale write at L57. There is no control showing the stale write succeeds when the touch is left out.","evidence":"L59-64: writeCode is any 40001/P2034 from anywhere in the callback.","impact":"The PASS may not prove that the 117 touch caused the abort.","recommended_fix":"Set a stage marker just before L57, require a serialization message or SQLSTATE 40001, and add a control run.","required_test":"Control run with 115 + function replace + bump but no touch: the stale write commits. Full 117: 40001 is raised at L57.","confidence":0.7},{"severity":"NIT","area":"Function ACL claim","file":"prisma/migrations/20261016050000_live_metric_order_upgrade_snapshot_fence/migration.sql","issue":"L50 claims the revoked ACL is preserved, but no test checks proacl, owner, prosecdef or proconfig.","evidence":"Neither harness reads pg_proc.","impact":"An ACL or definer regression would go unnoticed.","recommended_fix":"Snapshot the pg_proc fields and trigger bindings before and after the upgrade and compare them.","required_test":"Assert the fields are equal in both harnesses.","confidence":0.65},{"severity":"NIT","area":"Lock release evidence","file":"scripts/wp20-order-upgrade-load-disposable.mjs","issue":"The test shows writers are blocked during the migration, but not that they can write again after COMMIT. Plain reads during the lock are also unchecked.","evidence":"L63-74 has no write after the migration.","impact":"A lingering lock or session would not be caught.","recommended_fix":"After L75, run a writer with lock_timeout 150ms. During the lock, run a SELECT.","required_test":"Write succeeds after COMMIT. SELECT is not blocked during the lock.","confidence":0.6}]}
